finding.claim: On Cloud Foundry, env, heapdump and threaddump (which require EndpointPermissions.Full) are served from the standard /actuator path with no permission check. The permission gate only covers /cloudfoundryapplication, so an unauthenticated request succeeds when the operator has exposed these endpoints. Conditional on operator exposure config; the default exposure is health,info only. Possibly intentional design; confirm with Steeltoe owners.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request to the default base path, e.g. GET /actuator/env, on a Cloud Foundry deployment where Management:Endpoints:Actuator:Exposure includes env, heapdump, threaddump or *.
finding.sink: Serving Full-permission actuator endpoints via EndpointMiddleware.InvokeAsync (EndpointMiddleware.cs:53-82).

trace.note: Permission gate runs only if Platform.IsCloudFoundry && IsCloudFoundryEnabled && IsCloudFoundryRequest(path).
IsCloudFoundryRequest matches only the /cloudfoundryapplication prefix, so /actuator/* bypasses the gate.
CanInvoke: isAtCloudFoundryPath is false for /actuator paths.
Non-CF path returns isEnabled && isExposed, with no permission term.
CanInvoke true, so the endpoint handler runs.
env requires EndpointPermissions.Full, but that requirement is enforced only by the CF gate at CloudFoundrySecurityMiddleware.cs:89.

finding.guards_checked: Platform.IsCloudFoundry and IsCloudFoundryEnabled (CF gate); HasCloudFoundrySecurity (applies only to CF path); default Exposure = health,info (ConfigureManagementOptions.cs:82-85); EndpointOptions.RequiredPermissions default Restricted with Full only on env, heapdump, threaddump. Not checked: ConfigureActuatorsMiddlewareStartupFilter middleware ordering in every host configuration.

finding.claim: The loggers POST endpoint changes live log levels for any category but inherits the default RequiredPermissions of Restricted, so a read-tier CF token (read_basic_data only) can perform a state-changing operation. Low confidence: possibly matches upstream Spring Boot CF semantics.
finding.source: HTTP POST to .../loggers/{name} with JSON body {configuredLevel: ...}, from a client holding a Restricted-tier CF token.
finding.sink: Logger level mutation via the loggers endpoint handler.

trace.note: Level validated with LoggerLevels.StringToLogLevel; logger name not validated.
Default RequiredPermissions = Restricted, and Loggers has no override.
Restricted-tier token passes the gate for loggers.

finding.guards_checked: Level value validated against known log levels; endpoint exposure check; CF permission gate at Restricted tier. Logger name is unvalidated but only used as a category key.

finding.claim: Unvalidated Host and X-Forwarded-Proto request headers are concatenated into the requestUri that builds hypermedia _links in the JSON response. Impact is limited to the requester's own response unless a shared cache stores it; caching was not checked.
finding.source: Request headers Host and X-Forwarded-Proto on a request to the actuator root.
finding.sink: Link href values in the actuator hypermedia JSON response.

trace.note: X-Forwarded-Proto read raw from headers, with no allowlist.
requestUri built as scheme://Host + Path with no validation.
requestUri used to compute link paths and base URL.
Same concatenation pattern on the CF endpoint.

finding.guards_checked: None on header values. Host header is normalized by the server; no allowlist applied. Shared-cache behaviour not checked.

finding.claim: Heap-dump output path is predictable (second-resolution timestamp in the shared temp directory), so a local co-tenant could pre-create a symlink at the expected name. Unverified: whether the underlying dump tool follows symlinks was not checked. Local-only, low severity.
finding.source: Local co-tenant with write access to the shared temp directory, timing the dump.
finding.sink: Dump file creation at the generated path, then reading it back in HeapDumpEndpointMiddleware.

trace.note: fileName = name_timestamp, with no random component.
File.Exists check then stream of the file contents; file deleted at line 51.

finding.guards_checked: Name is server-generated, not attacker-chosen; heapdump endpoint requires Full on CF; not exposed by default. No random component or O_EXCL-style creation observed.
